'''Alan Bicksler Fowler''' (October 15, 1928 – August 4, 2024) was an American [[physicist]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Alan Bicksler Fowler |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/alan-bicksler-fowler |website=amacad.org |publisher=American Academy of Arts & Science |access-date=17 August 2021}}</ref>

==Life and education==
He was born in Denver, Colorado on October 15, 1928.<ref name="AIP"/> Fowler served in the U.S. Army from 1946 to 1948 and from 1952 to 1953.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alan Fowler|url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?fowlera|website=ACAP Array of Contemporary American Physicists|publisher=American Institute of Physics|access-date=2011-10-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222035019/https://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?fowlera|archive-date=2015-12-22|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He earned a BS in 1951, then an MS in 1952 from [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] in [[Troy, New York]]. In 1958, he earned his PhD from [[Harvard University]].<ref name="AIP"/>

Fowler was married to Kathleen Devlin for 65 years, until her death in 2016, with whom he had two sons and two daughters.<ref>{{cite web |title=KATHLEEN DEVLIN FOWLER 1928 - 2016 |url=https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/postgazette/obituary.aspx?n=kathleen-devlin-fowler&pid=180179024 |website=legacy.com |publisher=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette |access-date=15 August 2021}}</ref> He is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/05/13/us/60-new-members-elected-to-academy-of-sciences.html?pagewanted=all&src=pm| title=60 New Members Elected to Academy of Sciences| work= The New York Times| date= May 13, 1990}}</ref>

Fowler died on August 4, 2024, at the age of 95 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alan B. Fowler |url=https://www.pittsburghcremation.com/obituaries/alan-b-fowler/ |access-date=2024-10-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Career==
He worked as a researcher for [[Raytheon Technologies]], from 1953 to 1956,<ref name="AIP">{{cite web |title=Alan Fowler |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11509025.html |website=history.aip.org |publisher=American Institute of Physics |access-date=13 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/alan-fowler-11453/ |title=Alan B. Fowler|access-date=13 August 2021 |work=royalsociety.org |publisher=The Royal Society |location=London, England}}</ref> and for [[IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center]] from 1958 to 1993, and was a member of the IBM [[Mobile operating system|MOS]] research group.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bassett |first1=Ross Knox |title=To the Digital Age: Research Labs, Start-up Companies, and the Rise of MOS Technology |date=2007 |publisher=JHU Press |page=285 |isbn=9780801886393 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UUbB3d2UnaAC&pg=PA |access-date=15 August 2021}}</ref>

He is an IBM Fellow Emeritus.<ref name="AIP"/>

Fowler is named as a co-inventor in nine [[U.S. Patent]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Patents by Inventor Alan B. Fowler |url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/alan-b-fowler |website=patents.justia.com |publisher=Justia Patents |access-date=15 August 2021}}</ref>

Fowler was awarded the Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize by the [[American Physical Society]] in 1988.<ref name="AIP"/>
